title: OpenAI retires the DALL·E GPT in ChatGPT — ChatGPT Images takes over
subtitle: The original DALL·E built-in agent is being turned off today, ending a three-year run as ChatGPT's default image path and steering every user onto OpenAI's newer image system.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: OpenAI is switching off the official DALL·E GPT inside ChatGPT today, August 30. The built-in agent — pinned in the GPT sidebar since the launch of custom GPTs in late 2023 — will no longer accept prompts, and OpenAI has told users to download any images they want to keep before the deadline, without committing to keep the stored files available afterward. Image generation itself is not going away. Every ChatGPT tier, the free plan included, keeps access through the newer 'ChatGPT Images' system, and third-party custom GPTs that call the image tool are unaffected.

The mechanism matters more than the name change. DALL·E 3, which powered the retired GPT, was a standalone diffusion model bolted onto ChatGPT through a tool call. ChatGPT Images is the front door to OpenAI's newer multimodal image stack, the same one that already served most requests when users typed 'generate an image' into the main chat box. So for most people, the switch is invisible — the model in the background changed months ago; today the last shortcut to the old path gets removed.

The retirement fits a pattern OpenAI has repeated across the summer: consolidating branded legacy tools into the main ChatGPT surface, then deprecating the standalone entry points. The company sunset the original o3 reasoning model on August 26 after a 90-day migration window, and has been quietly narrowing the GPT store to steer users toward its own agent framework. Each of these moves reduces the surface area OpenAI has to support — and reduces the number of places a user can accidentally invoke an older, slower, or less-aligned model when a newer one is available.

Takeaway for learners: when a product you rely on gets 'consolidated,' the interesting question is not what disappeared but what quietly replaced it. If you built lesson plans, portfolio pieces, or research notebooks against the DALL·E GPT, download the artifacts now, and re-run one or two prompts against ChatGPT Images to see how the outputs differ — style, aspect ratio, and text rendering all shift between the two systems. Muscle-memory prompts written for the old model are the first thing to break.
